scenario: AITA for lying to my bf and letting him believe his ex cheated on him? | I know this sounds really bad but just hear me out. it's been eating me up inside so I'd like some feedback. We're currently college seniors and we started dating only 4 months ago. For his first two years he was dating another girl that I somewhat knew since we're in the same sorority but I wasn't close to. I had a crush on him since basically freshman year but I knew he was dating this girl. Anyways they ultimately broke up because he suspected she was cheating due to rumors about a party where she reportedly danced and kissed some guy. I was also there but I don't remember seeing her since it was a huge venue that was hosted by our sorority and we didn't really have overlapping friends circles. So when we started dating he was obviously still really torn up about his ex and questioning their break-up. It really stung to see him still so torn up about it, since all I wanted for us was a new start and for him to forget his ex completely. So when he asked me if I had seen his ex at that party, I don't know why but I lied and said that I had seen her with other guys. That really sealed it for him and I think he's moved on a lot faster. He says it's a no-brainer that they broke up because she cheated and now he knows for sure. He says he feels a lot better knowing that he didn't dump her for no reason. I know there's nothing to gain by telling the truth now. He's so much happier than before and he has no regrets about his exgf anymore. So, am I the asshole for lying and keeping up with the lie?

Relationships thrive on honesty, and even small lies can erode that foundation over time. If your boyfriend finds out later (and he might, especially if his ex or others confirm the truth), it could create deeper distrust than the original issue. 2. **The "greater good" defense is flawed** – While your goal was to help him heal, relationships aren’t just about emotional outcomes. The *how* matters as much as the *why*. If you had been honest from the start, he might have processed his feelings differently—but at least he wouldn’t be carrying the weight of a lie. 3. **The lie might backfire** – If his ex or others reveal the truth, he could feel betrayed *twice*: once by her (if she didn’t cheat) and once by you. Even if she did cheat, the lie could make him question whether you’re trustworthy in other areas of the relationship. 4. **Alternative approaches exist** – Instead of lying, you could have: - **Avoided the topic** (if you didn’t see her). - **Told the truth** (even if it was "I don’t remember seeing her, but I don’t know for sure"). - **Redirected his focus** (e.g., "Let’s talk about how we can make our relationship stronger instead of dwelling on the past"). 5. **His happiness isn’t worth the cost** – While he’s happier now, is that sustainable? If he later discovers the truth, the fallout could be worse than the initial pain of knowing she might not have cheated. Love isn’t just about feeling good in the moment—it’s about building a future together on honesty. 6. **You’re setting a precedent** – If you lie now, what stops you from lying in the future? Even if you don’t, your boyfriend might start questioning whether you’re being truthful in other areas. ### **But… there’s a silver lining** You’re clearly someone who cares deeply about your partner’s happiness. That’s a great quality! The key is to channel that care into *healthy* ways of supporting him—like being a safe space for him to process his feelings without fabricating stories. ### **What should you do now?** - **Don’t double down on the lie.** If he asks again, you’ll have to keep it up, which is unsustainable. - **Prepare for the truth.** If he ever finds out (and he might, especially if his ex or others confirm), be ready to own your mistake. Say something like: *"I’m sorry I lied to you. I thought it would help you move on, but I realize now that honesty is more important. I should have been upfront about what I saw (or didn’t see). I’m here to support you, no matter what."* - **Focus on rebuilding trust.** If he forgives you, use this as a chance to strengthen your communication. Say things like: *"I want us to always be able to talk about anything, even if it’s hard. I messed up by lying, but I’ll do better."* ### **Final Thought** You’re not the asshole for *feeling* conflicted—you’re the asshole for *acting* on it. But you can still be the person who grows from this and makes your relationship stronger. The fact that you’re asking this question shows you have integrity. Now, it’s about repairing what you’ve done. Would you like help brainstorming how to handle this conversation with your boyfriend if he ever finds out?
